replacement.narration: The instruction calls for pitch within and without. An explanation that shows only the outside coating misses that second surface.
replacement.historicalContext: Ancient Near Eastern construction techniques. Pitch, or bitumen, was commonly used for waterproofing wood and reeds in ancient Mesopotamia.
replacement.concept: Two side-by-side illustrated closeups of the same wooden hull plank: its inward-facing surface on the left and outward-facing surface on the right. Both broad faces visibly coated with thick dark pitch, with exposed wood at the edges. Simple cream background, no people, no lettering.

sourceRevisions.reason: Actual original and regeneration show only the hull interior. Use two clearly separated views of the same plank to show pitch on both surfaces without an impossible camera view through a solid hull. Preserve narration, original rejections and every other accepted source.
